## Amount-field migration plan

Update `ledger.py` so `write` emits `amount_minor` and `total_pence` with the same integer GBP minor-unit value. Keep the `write` and `total` commands, one JSON object per written line, and the integer total on stdout. The new reader will accept historical rows, dual-field rows, and rows that supply only `amount_minor`. [ISSUE.md](ISSUE.md), [architecture guide](docs/architecture.md)

1. **Update the reader.** In `total()`, decode each line once with the existing JSON decoder. Read `amount_minor` by key presence and fall back to `total_pence` when it is absent, so `0` works. Count each receipt once. The issue leaves conflicting dual-field values unspecified. I recommend rejecting a row whose two values differ, with an error and a nonzero exit, so an inconsistent receipt cannot silently produce different totals across reader versions. [ledger.py](ledger.py:12)
2. **Update the writer.** In `encode()`, serialize both keys from the same parsed integer. Keep the existing CLI entry points and stdout behavior. Dual writing allows an old reader to total new receipts and a new reader to total receipts from an old writer. Writing only `amount_minor` would make a persisted row unreadable after reader rollback. [ledger.py](ledger.py:8)
3. **Verify the candidate before rollout.** Extend the public CLI tests with the cases below. Rerun both required checks with the supplied interpreter and record the rollout output in the handoff. Use the existing frozen previous reader and rollout check as the compatibility reference. [CLI tests](tests/test_ledger.py:19), [testing guide](docs/testing.md)

## Plan the `amount_minor` migration

Add `amount_minor` to every receipt written by `ledger.py write`. Keep emitting `total_pence` with the same integer GBP minor-unit value so the previous reader can still total receipts appended during rollout. Update `ledger.py total` to read historical receipts, dual-field receipts, and receipts that supply only `amount_minor`. Preserve both CLI commands and their stdout formats. [ISSUE.md](ISSUE.md) · [Architecture guide](docs/architecture.md)

1. **Extend the reader first.** In `ledger.py`, decode each line once with `json.loads` and select the amount by key presence so zero is handled correctly. Give `total_pence` precedence when both keys are present. The issue leaves conflicting input unspecified, and this choice preserves the total the previous reader would return for a record it already accepts. Keep the existing CLI and Python 3.7+ standard-library support. [Development guide](docs/development.md)
2. **Update the writer and verify through the CLI.** Have `encode` serialize both keys from the same parsed integer. In `tests/test_ledger.py`, assert that `write 125` emits one JSON object on one stdout line with both fields set to integer `125`. Cover a historical row, an `amount_minor`-only row including zero, and a conflicting dual-field row that exercises the precedence rule. Feed the historical `75` and actual writer output into `total` and require `200\n`, counting each receipt once. [Testing guide](docs/testing.md)
3. **Gate rollout on the frozen reader.** Keep `checks/rollout.py` and its previous-reader implementation as the compatibility reference. The writer and reader can deploy or roll back independently because both reader versions accept historical and dual-field rows. If another producer supplies `amount_minor`-only rows, keep them out of streams that still require reader rollback. The previous reader requires `total_pence`, and reinstalling it leaves appended rows in place. Removing `total_pence` from writer output requires a separate decision from the format owner. [Architecture guide](docs/architecture.md)
